bc_transgression_wall.blurb: Transgression Wall is a small slab-style face within Kinnaird Bluffs, near Castlegar in the West Kootenays. It has five routes, four of them trad and one sport, spread from 5.6 up through the 5.10 range, with the 5.8 and 5.9 lines giving newer leaders a manageable option. Several lines finish on shared anchors, which makes top-roping practical, and there is a ground-level two-bolt anchor on the far left that suits practice sessions. The wall sits at roughly 635 m elevation, a short scramble above the Open Book Wall.

bc_sanitarium.blurb: Sanitarium is a compact sport crag in the Sanctuary zone above Squamish, with five bolted routes. Difficulty starts at 5.10 and tops out around 5.12, with most of the lines in the 5.11 band, so it suits climbers already comfortable on steeper, harder sport. The right-hand side of the cliff catches full sun. The trail to it splits off the main path to the Basement crag once you are across a dry creek bed. Expect a short day's worth of routes rather than a destination in itself, best paired with its neighbours in the Sanctuary.

bc_takakkaw_falls_area.blurb: This area in Yoho National Park, in the BC Rockies, is centred on Takakkaw Falls, a 1,260 ft waterfall often called the second highest in western Canada. It holds five climbs: four trad routes and one ice route. The summer line beside the falls is a 12-pitch outing at a moderate 5.7, and the other rock routes range from 5.7 to 5.9+. In winter the falls form a four-pitch WI4. The base sits near 1,524 m elevation, so snow lingers late and the cold season brings the ice into play.

bc_the_south_gulley_left_side.blurb: The South Gulley Left Side is a small sport crag in Williams Lake's Esler Bluffs, in the Cariboo. Five short bolted routes run from an easy 5.7 through a couple of 5.10s to one 5.11, so there is something for newer leaders and for climbers warming up on harder lines. It faces south, so it gets more sun than the bluffs' north-facing walls. A cave marks the spot along the trail, and the crag sits at about 918 m elevation.

bc_rfw_wall.blurb: RFW Wall is a small trad crag on the Arrow Lakes side of Castlegar, in the West Kootenays. All five routes fall in the 5.10 range, so it is for climbers already leading at that level. Climbs tend toward sustained liebacking, with natural gear low on the pitch and a couple of bolts near the top; a rack of small to medium nuts and cams, up to about a 3 inch cam, is enough. The walk up is short through forest, and the crag sits at about 495 m elevation with views over the water.
bc_rfw_wall.parking_note: Pull off on the left just beyond Scotty's Marina, then cross the road to the start of the trail.
bc_rfw_wall.approach: A short uphill walk through forest, next to a large boulder that carries a sign, then on a faint trail to the base of the wall.

bc_04_garden_wall.blurb: Garden Wall is a small crag among the Fairview (CIC) Bluffs above Nelson, number four in the bluffs' lower-to-upper numbering. It has five routes, mostly trad with one sport line, from 5.6 up to 5.10, so the grades lean easy to moderate. Moss tends to cover the wall, so expect to do some cleaning. It sits at about 724 m elevation, reached from the Svaboda Road end of the bluffs.
